then.text: The reading went beautifully. Somebody sneezed in the quiet bit, but that's live theatre.
Llareggub, the town in the play, is a rude word spelled backwards. Dylan thought he was very clever. He was.
All four! Captain Cat, Polly Garter, Organ Morgan and Mrs Ogmore-Pritchard. We've got our voices for the reading. Diolch yn fawr, thank you very much.
Here, take a copy of the play. And a lovespoon from the gift shop. Carved spoons are how Welsh lads courted, once. Don't read anything into it.

else.text: Still missing a voice or two. Captain Cat dreams by the boats, Polly Garter sings over her washing, Organ Morgan plays, and Mrs Ogmore-Pritchard polishes. Find them all.

Croeso to the Dylan Thomas Centre. Dylan wrote Under Milk Wood, a play for voices, about one spring day in a little Welsh seaside town called Llareggub.
It was first read on stage in New York in 1953, a few weeks before he died there, and first broadcast on the BBC in 1954. Sixty-odd voices, and nobody leaves the town.
We're putting on a reading and our actors are scattered across Swansea, rehearsing in all sorts of places. Could you find four of them for me?
Captain Cat, Polly Garter, Organ Morgan and Mrs Ogmore-Pritchard. Listen for them around town. Pob lwc, good luck!
